title: Dragon Mania Legends Energy, Void and Metal Dragon Combos | Plasma, Rain, Toxic, Dracula and More
description: Dragon Mania Legends breeding combos for Energy, Void and Metal dragons: Plasma, Meteor, Eel, Lightning, Razor, Rain, Lumino, Toxic and Dracula, plus how elements decide what you can breed. Combos checked on the DML wiki and the TouchTapPlay guide.

sections.heading: The advanced elements
sections.script: Welcome back to Dragon Mania Legends. In this guide we go beyond the starter elements and look at dragons with Energy, Void and Metal. These elements unlock some of the coolest designs in the game, but the rule for breeding them is the same as always. In Dragon Mania Legends you never pick the baby directly. You pick two parents, and the baby can only get elements that its parents carry. So the one rule to remember is simple: the two parents together must carry every element of the dragon you want. We will go from simple two element dragons to tough three element ones, and for each dragon you get the exact elements its parents need to carry.

sections.heading: Before you start
sections.script: Two quick reminders before the list. First, no combination in Dragon Mania Legends is guaranteed. The same parents can give you different dragons on different tries, because several dragons share the same elements. Second, the higher the level of your parents, and the rarer they are, the better your chances of a rare baby. So for the three element dragons near the end of this video, level up your parents before you start. That one habit saves a lot of time and a lot of frustration.

sections.heading: Plasma Dragon - Fire + Energy
sections.script: The Plasma Dragon carries Fire and Energy. To get it, breed two dragons that together carry Fire and Energy. Pair a Fire dragon with an Energy dragon, or hybrids that bring Fire and Energy. Watch out, because Fire and Energy are also the elements of the Meteor Dragon. So the same parents can give you either Plasma or Meteor, and you may need a few tries to land the one you want.

sections.heading: Meteor Dragon - Energy + Fire
sections.script: The Meteor Dragon carries Energy and Fire. To get it, breed two dragons that together carry Energy and Fire. Exactly the same elements as Plasma. That means one good pair of Fire and Energy parents works toward both dragons at once. If you want to collect both, keep that pair breeding, and every try is a chance at one of them. This is a great example of why it pays to know which dragons share elements.

sections.heading: Eel Dragon - Water + Energy
sections.script: The Eel Dragon carries Water and Energy. To get it, breed two dragons that together carry Water and Energy. Breed a Water dragon with an Energy dragon, or hybrids that carry Water and Energy between them. If you already have a strong Water parent from your Ice or Snow plans, you can reuse it here with an Energy partner. Reusing high level parents is one of the best ways to save time.

sections.heading: Lightning Dragon - Energy + Wind
sections.script: The Lightning Dragon carries Energy and Wind. To get it, breed two dragons that together carry Energy and Wind. Your two parents together must carry Energy and Wind. Check the elements of your hybrids carefully, and pick a pair that covers both. As with every dragon here, the result is not guaranteed, so give it a few tries with leveled up parents.

sections.heading: Razor Dragon - Metal + Wind
sections.script: The Razor Dragon carries Metal and Wind. To get it, breed two dragons that together carry Metal and Wind. Pair a Metal dragon with a Wind dragon, or hybrids that bring Metal and Wind. Metal is a great element to start building early, because it shows up again in some of the toughest dragons, including the Dracula Dragon later in this video.

sections.heading: Rain Dragon - Water + Void
sections.script: The Rain Dragon carries Water and Void. To get it, breed two dragons that together carry Water and Void. Now we step into Void. Breed a Water dragon with a Void dragon, or hybrids that carry Water and Void between them. Void opens up a whole new set of dragons, and Rain is a nice simple one to aim for first, since it only needs two elements.

sections.heading: Lumino Dragon - Fire + Void
sections.script: The Lumino Dragon carries Fire and Void. To get it, breed two dragons that together carry Fire and Void. Pair a Fire dragon with a Void dragon, or hybrids with Fire and Void. If you kept your Void parent from the Rain Dragon, swap the Water partner for a Fire one and you are set. Small changes like that let one strong parent work toward many goals.

sections.heading: Toxic Dragon - Plant + Energy + Void
sections.script: The Toxic Dragon carries Plant, Energy and Void. To get it, breed two dragons that together carry Plant, Energy and Void. Our first three element dragon. Your parents together must carry Plant, Energy and Void. A simple way to plan it is to use one parent that already carries two of those elements, and a second parent that brings the third. Three element dragons usually take more tries, so this is where leveled up parents really pay off.

sections.heading: Dracula Dragon - Void + Metal + Wind
sections.script: The Dracula Dragon carries Void, Metal and Wind. To get it, breed two dragons that together carry Void, Metal and Wind. Another three element dragon, and one of the coolest looking. Your parents together need Void, Metal and Wind. The Metal and Wind parent you planned for the Razor Dragon is a perfect starting point here: add a partner that brings Void, and all three elements are covered.

sections.heading: Why three element dragons take longer
sections.script: You may have noticed that Toxic and Dracula feel much harder than Plasma or Rain. Here is why. When your two parents carry more elements between them, more different dragons become possible from the same pair. Every extra possible result is another dragon that can hatch instead of the one you want. That is why three element dragons usually need more tries than two element ones. You cannot remove that randomness, but you can push the odds your way: use parents that carry exactly the elements you need, and level them up, because higher level and rarer parents give you better chances of a rare result.

sections.heading: Build a breeding plan
sections.script: Here is a simple plan that uses everything in this video. Start with the two element dragons, like Plasma, Eel, Razor, Rain and Lumino, because each one teaches you a new element pair and gives you new parents. Then look at what you have. A dragon with Metal and Wind, like Razor, is already two thirds of the way to Dracula. A dragon with Energy from your Plasma or Eel plans brings one of the three elements Toxic needs. Step by step, your two element dragons become the parents for your three element goals. Planning like this means every dragon you breed is useful later, even the ones that hatch by surprise.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
sections.script: Let's finish with three common mistakes. Mistake one: giving up on a combination after one or two tries. No combination is guaranteed, so a different result does not mean your pair is wrong. Mistake two: forgetting to check the elements. If one element is missing from both parents, that dragon cannot hatch from that pair, no matter how many times you try. Mistake three: breeding with low level parents for a rare dragon. Level up first, because higher level and rarer parents improve your odds.

sections.heading: Recap
sections.script: Quick recap. Plasma and Meteor both need Fire and Energy. Eel needs Water and Energy. Lightning needs Energy and Wind. Razor needs Metal and Wind. Rain needs Water and Void, and Lumino needs Fire and Void. For the big ones, Toxic needs Plant, Energy and Void, and Dracula needs Void, Metal and Wind. Remember, no combination is guaranteed, and higher level, rarer parents give you better odds. Which dragon should I cover next? Let me know in the comments, and subscribe for more Dragon Mania Legends guides.
